results.title: Are BCN Climate Shelters accessible to vulnerable residents?
results.content: # Are Barcelona’s climate shelters accessible to vulnerable residents? A new study led by @Serena Mombelli, a PhD researcher at the @GEMOTT research group on mobility, transport and territory at the Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona, ​​has been published in the journal Cities. The study was conducted during her research visit to the @Data Analytics & Visualization Group at the @Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC-CNS), as part of the @vCity project. The study examines whether Barcelona’s Climate Shelter Network provides equitable access for its most vulnerable residents. This research is part of wider efforts to understand how mobility and social inequalities interact with urban climate adaptation strategies. The authors used GIS-based isochrone analysis and socioeconomic data to evaluate the spatial and temporal accessibility of shelters within a 10-minute walking distance, accounting for slower walking speeds of 3.28 km/h. The findings provide evidence-based guidance for Barcelona’s 2030 goal of ensuring that everyone has access to a shelter within five minutes and offer a framework for evaluating climate adaptation equity in other urban contexts.

Title: Health and Lifestyle of Older Adults: Global Trends in an Aging Population - Measuredhs
Home BlogHealth and Lifestyle of Older Adults: Global Trends in an Aging Population. # Health and Lifestyle of Older Adults: Global Trends in an Aging Population. According to the United Nations, the global population of older adults is projected to reach 2.1 billion by 2050, more than doubling from 2020 figures. Several key factors are fueling the aging of the world’s population. Countries with aging populations must allocate more resources to long-term care, hospital infrastructure, and trained geriatric professionals. Unfortunately, geriatric care is underdeveloped in many LMICs, where the aging population is growing the fastest. The lifestyle of older adults is influenced by a variety of factors, including income, culture, urbanization, and social support. Mental health is a critical yet often overlooked component of older adults’ well-being. Research consistently shows that older adults who maintain strong social connections and engage in community activities experience better mental and physical health outcomes. Technology is increasingly shaping the health and lifestyle of older adults. Many older adults lack digital literacy or access to reliable internet services. Recognizing the implications of aging populations, global institutions are calling for policy reforms and innovation. The World Health Organization (WHO) has declared 2021–2030 the “Decade of Healthy Ageing,” urging countries to invest in age-friendly environments, integrated care, and long-term support systems. Japan, with the world’s oldest population, has implemented comprehensive aging policies that include pension reform, elder employment initiatives, and investments in robotic care technology. Scandinavian countries have adopted universal long-term care models that provide equitable access to services for older adults. Community health workers, family-based care models, and policies that empower older adults as active contributors—not just recipients—of care will be crucial. Global aging is not a distant phenomenon—it is already reshaping economies, health systems, and communities. With the right investments in healthcare, social infrastructure, and inclusive policy, older adults can lead healthier, more fulfilling lives well into their later years. Almost one in ten older adults currently lives in poverty, leading to higher healthcare needs while restricting access to necessary services. Enhancing social support and healthcare access is vital for improving older adults’ quality of life. Innovative Solutions for Healthcare Accessibility Healthcare IT is essential in improving service delivery for older adults. Transforming Workflow with AI Solutions Enhanced Efficiency and Patient Engagement through AI To address the challenges posed by the aging population, healthcare administrators should consider adopting AI technologies like Simbo AI. Moreover, AI can analyze data from patient interactions to identify trends related to healthcare access and the challenges faced by older adults. Addressing Health Disparities with AI Solutions The use of AI in healthcare can also help reduce disparities in access to care among underserved populations. By addressing these disparities, healthcare administrators can allocate resources more effectively, implement outreach programs, and improve health outcomes for older adults. The Future of Healthcare for Older Adults As the healthcare system evolves in response to an aging population, providers and administrators must be proactive in their service delivery methods. Addressing the demands of an aging population is important for creating a healthcare system that benefits older adults and society.
